title: NATO Ankara Summit Opens as Trump Muses Cutting European Troop Presence by a Third
detail: The NATO Leaders' Summit opened in Ankara, Turkey on July 7, 2026, with President Trump renewing his demand that the US take control of Greenland and floating the idea of cutting the American troop presence in Europe by as much as one-third to send a message to the alliance on burden-sharing. Trump argued Greenland is surrounded by Chinese and Russian ships and framed a deeper US drawdown as leverage over allies who have not matched Washington's spending or Iran-war support. The remarks set a combative tone ahead of two days of talks on defense spending, Ukraine aid, and Article 5 credibility.

media.caption: Trump renews Greenland threats at NATO summit, says US could remove troops from Europe

title: NATO Unveils $40 Billion 'Drone Edge' Counter-Drone Initiative at Ankara Summit
detail: NATO allies announced on July 7, 2026 that they will invest more than $40 billion over five years to expand counter-drone defenses, drone procurement, and operator training under the new 'Drone Edge Initiative,' launched by Secretary General Mark Rutte. The package establishes a NATO-tested, NATO-compatible counter-drone marketplace, aims to train five times as many drone operators by the end of 2027 via NATO Flight Training Europe, and expands surveillance-drone procurement through the NATO Support and Procurement Agency. It marks a shift from isolated national counter-drone efforts toward a coordinated alliance-wide approach.

media.caption: NATO approves $40 billion counter-drone initiative to defeat low-cost UAV threats
